data.tombstone: Landscape with Peasants Dancing, c. 1645–50. David Teniers (Flemish, 1610–1690). Oil on wood; framed: 69 x 96.5 x 8 cm (27 3/16 x 38 x 3 1/8 in.); unframed: 49 x 78 cm (19 5/16 x 30 11/16 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of the Frances W. Ingalls Trust, 1996.271
data.title: Landscape with Peasants Dancing

provenance.description: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Cleveland, Ohio
Frances W. Ingalls [1926-1996], Cleveland, OH, given to the Cleveland Museum of Art
Jane Taft Ingalls [1874-1962], Cleveland, OH, by descent to her daughter-in-law, Frances W. Ingalls
Rosenberg & Stiebel, New York, NY, sold to Jane Taft Ingalls
Baron Louis de Rothschild [1882-1955], East Barnard, VT, sold to Rosenberg & Stiebel
In possession of the United States Forces in Austria (USFA), restituted to Louis de Rothschild
footnotes: The painting was recovered by the Allies at the Alt Ausee salt mine, where it had been hidden by the Nazis, and then sent to the Munich Central Collecting Point (Alt Aussee shipment no. 2777), arriving on July 13, 1945 and assigned Munich number 4040 (4040/Aussee 2777.  3723 Aussee 2461 - 4136 Aussee 2873.  Records Relating to Property Accessions, compiled 1945 – 1949.  Records Concerning the Central Collecting Points ("Ardelia Hall Collection"): Munich Central Collecting Point, 1945-1951, Record Group 260.  National Archives Identifier 3725277.  M1946, Roll 173, page 1.  Fold3.com, http://www.fold3.com/image/312557487/, retrieved January 22, 2015).  According to the records of the Collecting Point and secondary sources, the painting, titled “Peasants Inn with Landscape,” was repatriated to Austria on May 16, 1946, and then restituted to Louis de Rothschild on September 28 of that year.

provenance.description: In possession of the Nazis; selected by Hitler for the Führermuseum, Linz
footnotes: Confiscated by the Nazis in 1938 from Louis de Rothschild’s collection in Vienna, this painting was selected by Hitler to be part of his planned Führermuseum in Linz.  It appears as no. 17, Landschaft mit Bauerntanz (49:78), in Album II of Hitler’s Gemäldegalerie Linz Album, which catalogued the works intended for the museum. It is also listed as seized from Louis de Rothschild (inv. LR 3) in the Vorschlag zur Verteilung der in Wien beschlagnahmte Gemälde: Für das Kunstmuseum in Linz of October 20, 1939, and the Verzeichnis der für Linz in Aussicht genommenen Gemälde of July 31, 1940, both prepared by Hans Posse, special envoy for the Linz Museum (Vorschlag zur Verteilung der in Wien beschlagnahmte Gemälde: Für das Kunstmuseum in Linz October 20, 1939. Linz Museum: Consolidated Interrogation Report (CIR) No. 4 (Attachments 56-82). Restitution Research Records. Records of the U.S. Occupation Headquarters, World War II, Record Group 260. National Archives Identifier 3725274. M1946, Roll 139, page 71. Fold3.com, http://www.fold3.com/image/#283755710, retrieved July 15, 2013, and Verzeichnis der für Linz in Aussicht genommenen Gemälde July 31, 1940. Linz Museum: Consolidated Interrogation Report (CIR) No. 4 (Attachments 56-82). Restitution Research Records. Records of the U.S. Occupation Headquarters, World War II, Record Group 260. National Archives Identifier 3725274. M1946, Roll 139, page 83. Fold3.com, http://www.fold3.com/image/#283755722, retrieved July 15, 2013).  The painting was stored at the monastery in Kremsmünster (Felicitas Kunth, Die Rothschild'schen Gemäldesammlungen in Wien, 2006) and then moved to the salt mine at Alt Aussee toward the end of the war.

data.did_you_know: This painting combines two of David Teniers's specialties: landscape and scenes of country life.
data.description: Before a rustic inn, a group of villagers converse, embrace, and dance to a bagpiper’s tune. Teniers was one of many Netherlandish artists whose paintings celebrate the joys of country life. These delicately painted works were created primarily for an elite urban audience nostalgic for a simpler existence.
